title: Direct Identifiability from Registration Data
description: Parent user provides directly identifying information (email, name, government ID) during registration, making them easily identifiable from this data flow.
assumptions: Registration data includes personally identifiable information (PII)

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Sensitive Registration Data
description: Sensitive registration data (password, government ID, six-digit code) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission or storage at the authentication service.
assumptions: Data is transmitted and stored without adequate encryption or access controls

title: Linkability of Registration Data to Other User Activities
description: Registration data could be linked to other user activities or data within the system, creating a comprehensive user profile.
assumptions: System maintains multiple data points about users that can be correlated

title: User Unawareness of Data Collection Scope
description: Parent user may not be fully aware of what data is being collected, how it will be used, or with whom it will be shared during registration.
assumptions: Privacy notice or consent mechanism may not clearly communicate data practices

title: Non-compliance with Privacy Regulations
description: Collection of government ID and other sensitive data may require compliance with GDPR, COPPA, or other privacy regulations that could be violated.
assumptions: System operates in jurisdiction with privacy regulations requiring specific handling of PII

title: Data Aggregation Creating Enhanced User Profile
description: Registration data could be aggregated with other user data to create a more complete profile than the user intended or consented to.
assumptions: System collects and stores multiple data points about users

title: Non-repudiation of Registration Actions
description: Parent user could deny having performed the registration if proper audit trails or authentication logs are not maintained by the authentication service.
assumptions: System may not maintain comprehensive audit logs of registration events

title: Unauthorized access to stored parent account data
description: The Authentication Service stores parent account information in MongoDB. If access controls are insufficient or the database is compromised, unauthorized parties could access sensitive parent account data including authentication credentials and user information.
assumptions: MongoDB instance has standard security configuration; parent account data includes PII or authentication-sensitive information

title: Excessive data collection for parent accounts
description: The Authentication Service may store more parent account data than necessary for authentication purposes, violating data minimization principles. This could include unnecessary personal identifiers or metadata that enable profiling.
assumptions: Parent account storage includes fields beyond strict authentication requirements

title: Users unaware of parent account data storage
description: Users may not be informed that their parent account information is being stored in MongoDB, or what specific data elements are collected and retained. This lack of transparency prevents informed consent.
assumptions: Privacy policy or consent mechanisms do not clearly disclose parent account data storage practices

title: Non-compliance with data retention requirements
description: Parent account data stored in MongoDB may be retained longer than necessary or without proper legal basis, potentially violating GDPR, CCPA, or other privacy regulations regarding data minimization and storage limitation.
assumptions: No automated data retention policies or deletion mechanisms are in place for parent account data

title: Linkability of JWT and user data
description: The JWT token combined with user data sent to the parent user could be linked across multiple authentication sessions to track user behavior and create a comprehensive activity profile.
assumptions: JWT contains session identifiers and user data includes personal information

title: Identifiability of parent user
description: The JWT and user data transmitted to the parent user could directly identify the parent, potentially exposing their identity to unauthorized parties if intercepted.
assumptions: JWT contains user identifiers and user data includes personally identifiable information

title: Unauthorized disclosure of authentication data
description: The JWT and user data could be intercepted during transmission from the Authentication Service to the Parent User, exposing sensitive authentication credentials and personal information.
assumptions: Data is transmitted over network without adequate encryption or security controls

title: Data aggregation across authentication flows
description: Multiple authentication data flows to the parent user could be aggregated to build a comprehensive profile of the parent's authentication patterns, access times, and associated user data.
assumptions: Multiple authentication sessions occur over time with consistent data patterns

title: Parent user unawareness of data transmission
description: The parent user may not be fully aware of what specific data is being transmitted to them via the JWT and user data flow, or how this data will be used.
assumptions: User consent and transparency mechanisms are not clearly implemented

title: Linkability of child authentication data
description: JWT containing userType 'child' combined with child profiles could be linked across sessions or services to track the child's activities and build behavioral profiles.
assumptions: JWT and profile data contain persistent identifiers that can be correlated

title: Identifiability of child user
description: Child profiles transmitted to the child user may contain personally identifiable information that could expose the child's identity if intercepted or mishandled.
assumptions: Child profiles contain PII such as name, age, or other identifying attributes

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child data
description: JWT and child profile data transmitted from Authentication Service to child user could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be fully encrypted or could be vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks

title: Data aggregation from child profiles
description: Child profile data combined with JWT authentication tokens could be aggregated with other data sources to create comprehensive child profiles beyond intended scope.
assumptions: Multiple data sources exist that could be combined with this flow's data

title: Child unawareness of data processing
description: Child users may not understand what personal data is being transmitted to them or how it will be used, especially given their age and capacity to comprehend privacy implications.
assumptions: Child users lack full capacity to understand data processing implications

title: Child profile data linking across systems
description: The combination of child's name, DOB, gender, and government ID creates quasi-identifiers that could be used to link this child's data with other data sources, enabling unwanted profiling or tracking across different systems.
assumptions: Child profile data may be stored or shared with other systems that could perform data linkage

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child profile information
description: Sensitive child profile data (name, DOB, gender, government ID) transmitted from parent to system could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties during the data flow.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be fully encrypted or protected

title: Unauthorized access to child profile creation flow
description: Unauthorized actors could gain access to the data flow and intercept or view the child profile information being submitted by the parent.
assumptions: Access controls on the data flow may be insufficient

title: Non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Collection of government ID and sensitive child information may violate child privacy regulations (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K) if proper consent, age verification, or data minimization measures are not implemented.
assumptions: System may not have adequate compliance measures for child data collection
uncertainty_note: Specific regulatory requirements depend on jurisdiction and system implementation

title: Unauthorized access to child profile data
description: Child profile data stored in MongoDB could be accessed by unauthorized parties if database access controls are insufficient, authentication is weak, or the database is misconfigured.
assumptions: MongoDB instance has proper security configuration; access controls are implemented

title: Excessive data collection in child profiles
description: The child profile management process may store more personal data than necessary, violating the minimality principle. This could include unnecessary fields that increase privacy risk without providing value.
assumptions: Data minimization principles are applied during profile design

title: Child identifiability from stored profile data
description: Child profile data may contain or enable identification of the child through direct identifiers (name, DOB) or indirect identifiers (unique combinations of attributes), especially if data is accessed or leaked.
assumptions: Profile contains identifying information about the child

title: Linkability of child profile with other data sources
description: Child profile data could be linked with other data (activity logs, location data, usage patterns) to create a more comprehensive profile, increasing privacy risks beyond what was intended.
assumptions: Other data sources exist that could be correlated with child profiles

title: Non-compliance with children's privacy regulations
description: Storing child profile data may not comply with applicable regulations (e.g., COPPA, GDPR-K) regarding consent, data retention, parental rights, and age-appropriate data handling.
assumptions: System operates in jurisdiction with children's privacy laws

title: Child activity data used for unintended purposes
description: Video search, like, and comment data from child users could be used for targeted advertising, profiling, or other purposes beyond the stated video management service functionality. Child data is particularly sensitive and requires strict purpose limitation.
assumptions: Video management service processes child user data for video interaction features

title: Child unaware of data collection scope
description: Child users may not understand what personal data is being collected through video search, requests, likes, and comments, or how this data will be used, stored, or shared. Children have limited capacity to provide informed consent.
assumptions: Child users interact with the video management service without full comprehension of privacy implications

title: Non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Processing child user data requires compliance with regulations such as COPPA, GDPR-K, or other child-specific privacy laws. The video management service may not have appropriate safeguards, parental consent mechanisms, or data minimization practices in place.
assumptions: Video management service processes data from users under applicable age thresholds for child protection laws

title: Unauthorized disclosure of child personal data
description: Child's video preferences, search history, likes, and comments could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties through data breaches, improper sharing, or inadequate access controls.
assumptions: Video management service stores and processes child user interaction data

title: Linkability of child activities across sessions
description: Child's video search, like, and comment activities could be linked across different sessions and time periods to build a comprehensive behavioral profile, potentially revealing sensitive interests or patterns.
assumptions: Video management service maintains persistent user accounts or tracking mechanisms

title: Identified information in video metadata
description: Video metadata stored in MongoDB may contain identifying information such as user IDs, timestamps, device identifiers, or location data that could be used to identify individuals.
assumptions: Video metadata includes user-identifying fields as is common in video management systems

title: Implicit data disclosure through metadata storage
description: Storing video metadata and files in MongoDB may result in implicit disclosure of personal data beyond what is strictly necessary, especially if metadata contains derived or inferred information about users.
assumptions: Metadata storage includes more than minimal required data

title: Linkability of video data across contexts
description: Video metadata stored in MongoDB could enable linking of user activities across different contexts or time periods, potentially revealing patterns of behavior.
assumptions: Metadata contains fields that can be used to correlate user activities

title: Child activity data linkable across systems
description: Child search and watch history stored in DS2 could be linked with other child profile data (e.g., age, location, preferences) to create comprehensive behavioral profiles, enabling tracking across different system components.
assumptions: Child profile data exists in other datastores or processes that could be correlated with search/watch history

title: Children identifiable from stored activity history
description: Search and watch history may contain personally identifiable information or patterns that could identify specific children, especially when combined with other profile data in the childprofiles collection.
assumptions: Search/watch history contains unique patterns or PII that could identify individual children

title: Unauthorized access to child activity data
description: MongoDB datastore containing child search and watch history could be accessed by unauthorized parties through database vulnerabilities, misconfigurations, or compromised credentials.
assumptions: Datastore security controls may have vulnerabilities or misconfigurations

title: Children/parents unaware of activity tracking
description: Children and their guardians may not be fully aware that search and watch history is being stored, or may not understand the extent of data collection and its implications.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly communicate activity tracking practices

title: Excessive collection of child behavioral data
description: Storing comprehensive search and watch history may exceed what is necessary for the service's core functionality, violating data minimization principles for children's data.
assumptions: Full search/watch history may not be strictly required for service operation
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific business requirements and legal obligations

title: Video uploads linked to parent user identity
description: The Video Management Service can link uploaded videos to specific parent users, enabling creation of user profiles and tracking of upload patterns over time.
assumptions: Video uploads contain metadata or are associated with user accounts

title: Parent user identifiability through video content
description: Parent user identity may be exposed through video metadata, embedded information, or content that reveals personal details about the uploader.
assumptions: Video files may contain identifying metadata or content

title: Unauthorized disclosure of video content
description: Video content or metadata could be accessed by unauthorized parties through the Video Management Service, potentially exposing sensitive information.
assumptions: Video content may contain sensitive or private information

title: Non-compliance with privacy regulations for video data
description: Video upload and approval process may not comply with applicable privacy regulations (e.g., COPPA, GDPR) regarding consent, data minimization, or purpose limitation for parent and child data.
assumptions: Video content may involve children's data requiring special protection
uncertainty_note: Context suggests parent users uploading videos, which may involve children's data requiring regulatory compliance

title: Unauthorized interception of video stream
description: The video stream sent from the Video Management Service to the child user could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission, potentially exposing the child to inappropriate content or revealing viewing patterns.
assumptions: Video stream is transmitted over network without adequate encryption or security measures

title: Aggregation of child viewing data
description: Data from multiple video streaming sessions could be aggregated to build detailed profiles of the child's viewing habits, preferences, and behavioral patterns, which could be used for targeted advertising or other purposes.
assumptions: Video service collects and stores viewing metadata across sessions

title: Child unaware of data collection during streaming
description: The child user may not be aware that data is being collected during video streaming (e.g., viewing history, device information, interaction patterns), and may not understand the implications of this data collection.
assumptions: Privacy notices are not child-friendly or are not presented in an understandable manner

title: Non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Streaming video to children may violate child privacy regulations such as COPPA if proper parental consent, data minimization, and age-appropriate privacy protections are not implemented.
assumptions: Service may not have adequate mechanisms for parental consent or age verification
uncertainty_note: Citation based on general child privacy regulation knowledge; specific regulatory requirements may vary by jurisdiction

title: Child browsing data disclosed to AI engine
description: Personal browsing data from child profiles is being transferred from the MongoDB datastore to the AI Recommendation Engine. This represents an explicit data disclosure that should be evaluated against the minimality principle - only strictly required data should be shared.
assumptions: The childprofiles collection contains personal browsing data that is identifiable to specific children.

title: Identifiable child data exposed to AI processing
description: Child profile data being sent to the AI engine may contain or enable identification of specific children, creating identifiability risks when combined with browsing patterns.
assumptions: The childprofiles collection contains identifiers or quasi-identifiers that could link browsing data to specific children.

title: Linkability of browsing patterns to child profiles
description: Browsing data transferred to the AI engine could be linked to create detailed behavioral profiles of individual children, enabling tracking across sessions and activities.
assumptions: The AI engine processes and stores browsing data in a way that maintains linkability to child profiles.

title: Children/guardians unaware of AI data processing
description: Children and their guardians may not be aware that browsing data is being sent to an AI recommendation engine for processing, violating transparency principles.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain AI-based processing of child browsing data.

title: Potential non-compliance with child privacy regulations
description: Transfer of child browsing data to AI engine may not comply with regulations like COPPA or GDPR-K, which have strict requirements for processing children's personal data.
assumptions: The system operates in a jurisdiction with child privacy protections requiring explicit consent and data minimization.
uncertainty_note: Regulatory compliance depends on specific jurisdiction and implementation details not fully specified.

title: Explicit Data Disclosure to Third-Party Advertisers
description: Browsing data is intentionally transferred from the AI Recommendation Engine to third-party advertisers, constituting an explicit data disclosure. This may violate data minimality principles if the shared data exceeds what is strictly necessary for advertising purposes.
assumptions: Browsing data contains personal information; transfer is intentional and planned.

title: User Identifiability via Browsing Data
description: Browsing data shared with advertisers may allow identification of individual users, especially if combined with other datasets or if the data includes unique identifiers.
assumptions: Browsing data contains or can be linked to personally identifiable information.

title: Linkability of User Activities
description: Shared browsing data may enable advertisers to link different user activities across sessions or services, creating detailed user profiles.
assumptions: Browsing data includes behavioral patterns that can be correlated over time.

title: User Unawareness of Data Sharing
description: Users may not be adequately informed that their browsing data is shared with third-party advertisers, violating transparency principles.
assumptions: No explicit user consent or notification mechanism is in place for this data flow.

title: Non-Compliance with Data Protection Regulations
description: Transferring browsing data to third-party advertisers may violate regulations like GDPR if proper legal bases (e.g., consent) are not established.
assumptions: Data transfer occurs without explicit user consent or other lawful basis.
uncertainty_note: Assumes no compliance measures are in place; actual compliance status unknown.

title: Unnecessary storage of government ID images
description: Government ID images are highly sensitive personal data. Storing them in a file system may violate the minimality principle if these images are not strictly required for the authentication service's function. This represents an avoidable data disclosure.
assumptions: The authentication service may not need to persistently store ID images; they could be processed and discarded after verification.

title: Unauthorized access to stored government ID images
description: If the file system (backend/uploads/) is compromised or lacks proper access controls, stored government ID images could be disclosed to unauthorized parties. This is a direct disclosure threat to highly sensitive personal data.
assumptions: The file system may not have adequate encryption, access controls, or security measures in place.

title: Direct identifiability through government ID images
description: Government ID images directly identify individuals and contain multiple identifying attributes (photo, name, ID number, etc.). Storing these images creates a high identifiability risk if the data is accessed or leaked.
assumptions: The ID images contain full identifying information without pseudonymization or anonymization.

title: Potential regulatory non-compliance for ID image storage
description: Storing government ID images may violate data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR) regarding data minimization, storage limitation, and special category data handling. This could result in compliance violations.
assumptions: The system operates in a jurisdiction with data protection regulations that apply to government ID data.
uncertainty_note: Regulatory requirements may vary by jurisdiction; this assumes GDPR-like regulations apply.

title: JWT enables cross-session user tracking
description: The JWT stored in localStorage contains user identity information that can be used to link user activities across different sessions, pages, or time periods, enabling behavioral tracking and profiling.
assumptions: JWT contains user identifiers and is accessible to scripts on the same domain

title: JWT exposes user identity in browser storage
description: Storing the JWT in localStorage makes user identity information accessible to any script running on the same domain, potentially exposing identifying information to malicious actors or third-party scripts.
assumptions: localStorage is accessible to all scripts on the domain and JWT contains identifying claims

title: JWT disclosure through XSS or browser extensions
description: JWTs stored in localStorage are vulnerable to disclosure through cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks, malicious browser extensions, or other client-side vulnerabilities that can read localStorage contents.
assumptions: Application may be vulnerable to XSS or user has malicious extensions installed

title: Users unaware of authentication token storage
description: Users may not be aware that their authentication tokens are being stored in browser localStorage, nor understand the privacy implications of this storage mechanism.
assumptions: No explicit user notification or consent mechanism for localStorage usage

title: Excessive Child History Information Disclosure
description: The child history data sent to the parent may contain more detailed or sensitive information than necessary for parental review, potentially revealing private aspects of the child's activities, communications, or location that should remain confidential.
assumptions: Child history includes detailed activity logs, location data, or communication records beyond what is needed for basic parental oversight

title: Child Profile Linking Across Data Sources
description: Child history data transmitted to the parent could be combined with other data sources to build a comprehensive profile of the child's behavior, preferences, and activities, potentially revealing patterns not intended to be disclosed.
assumptions: Parent or third parties may aggregate this data with other child-related information from different systems

title: Unauthorized Access to Child History in Transit
description: Child history data could be intercepted by unauthorized parties during transmission from the process to the parent user, exposing sensitive information about the child's activities.
assumptions: Data transmission may not be properly encrypted or secured against interception

title: Child History Data Theft
description: The child history data could be stolen during transmission, potentially leading to misuse of sensitive information about the child's activities, location, or behavior patterns.
assumptions: Inadequate security controls on the data flow between process and external entity
